title: Board Portfolio Performance Capstone
context: DataQuest Holdings asks you to review standardized synthetic KPI snapshots from its e-commerce, SaaS, banking, hospital-operations and logistics businesses. Build a decision-ready comparison without pretending that cross-company associations prove causation.
cleaningPrompt: Which controls should be completed before comparing companies? Select all required actions.
cleaningOptions: Validate service_score and exception_rate are plausible percentages and operating/volume indexes are positive.
Standardize company and period labels before grouping.
Delete the lowest-performing company so it does not distort the portfolio average.
Replace every high operating-cost index with 100.
cleaningExpectedSelections: Validate service_score and exception_rate are plausible percentages and operating/volume indexes are positive.
Standardize company and period labels before grouping.
sqlPrompt: Using capstone_company_kpis, return company_key and ROUND(MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'Current' THEN service_score END) - MAX(CASE WHEN period = 'Baseline' THEN service_score END), 1) AS service_change grouped by company_key.
statisticsPrompt: Hospital and logistics show larger service-score gains while also showing larger operating-cost increases. What is the strongest statistical interpretation?
statisticsOptions: The pattern is an association worth investigating, but it does not prove higher operating cost caused the service improvement; company mix and operating changes may confound the relationship.
Higher operating cost definitely caused every service-score improvement.
The relationship should be ignored because descriptive comparisons are never useful.
Remove hospital and logistics before analysis because their changes are larger.
statisticsExpected: The pattern is an association worth investigating, but it does not prove higher operating cost caused the service improvement; company mix and operating changes may confound the relationship.
kpiPrompt: The current service scores are 88, 91, 89, 86 and 84. What is the portfolio average current service score?
dashboardPrompt: Which executive visual best compares baseline versus current service score across all five companies?
dashboardOptions: Grouped bar or dumbbell chart with company on the axis and baseline/current service score clearly paired
Five separate pie charts with service score as a slice
A single gauge that hides company-level variation
A scatter plot with company names treated as numeric time
dashboardExpected: Grouped bar or dumbbell chart with company on the axis and baseline/current service score clearly paired
recommendationPrompt: Which board recommendation is most defensible from this synthetic portfolio review?
recommendationOptions: Preserve the broad service improvements, prioritize logistics and hospital for deeper cost/exception driver analysis, and test targeted operating changes before scaling because the portfolio comparison does not establish causality.
Cut every company to the same operating-cost index immediately.
Invest only in the company with the highest current service score and ignore volume or exception rates.
Claim that higher cost caused better service across the portfolio.
recommendationExpected: Preserve the broad service improvements, prioritize logistics and hospital for deeper cost/exception driver analysis, and test targeted operating changes before scaling because the portfolio comparison does not establish causality.
